newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein moves into N.Ireland talks office.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein moves into N.Ireland talks office.

text.p: Officials of Sinn Fein, led by convicted Irish republican bomber Gerry Kelly, arrived at Belfast's Stormont buildings on Monday and took possession of offices for Northern Ireland peace talks.
It was the first time Sinn Fein had been allowed to enter the venue of the negotiations and was permitted in the wake of the weekend ceasefire by its IRA (Irish Republican Army) guerrilla allies.

Kelly, who served a jail term for bombing London's Old Bailey court complex in 1972, said he and his aides had come to occupy their offices and hoped to hold preliminary talks with other parties to the negotiations.
He said Mitchell McLaughlin, chairman of the party which shares the IRA goal of ending British rule of Northern Ireland, would be arriving later.
Kelly is a senior official in Sinn Fein. He escaped from a British jail in the 1980s and was extradited from the Netherlands.
He has been on the party's negotiating team since returning to Belfast.
